title: No One Best Way to Manage? | Principles of Management Ep 13
description:
Ravi's long team chats work beautifully on a slow afternoon at Chai Corner. But in the morning rush, thirty customers wait and their chai goes cold. On festival day he does the opposite: quick, firm orders, one job each, and the queue keeps moving. In this animated lesson we use his chai stall to understand the contingency approach: there is no one best way to manage, because it all depends on the situation.

You will learn what contingent means and how the idea grew from 1960s research: Burns and Stalker (1961) on strict versus flexible firms, Joan Woodward (1965) and her study of one hundred factories, Lawrence and Lorsch (1967) on the environment, and Fred Fiedler on leaders who fit the situation. We then run the same morning rush two ways, team chat against firm orders, and watch the queue and the waiting time change. We cover the four things the right way depends on (size, technology, environment and people), see contingency thinking at work in banks, startups, emergency rooms, phone makers and hospitals, and look honestly at its limits: no ready answer, and a manager can read the situation wrong.

This is Episode 13 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
